author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
review: 'The Great Gatsby' is a timeless masterpiece delving into the decadence and disillusionment of the Jazz Age. Set in the Roaring Twenties, it follows Jay Gatsby's lavish parties masking his obsession with lost love, offering a critique of wealth and the elusive American Dream.

author: Harper Lee
review: Set in the American South, this Pulitzer Prize-winning novel explores racial injustice and childhood innocence through the eyes of young Scout Finch. Her father, Atticus Finch, stands as a moral compass defending an innocent man against deep-seated prejudice.

author: George Orwell
review: A chilling dystopian classic warning against totalitarian regimes, pervasive surveillance, and psychological manipulation. Winston Smith struggles for individuality and truth under the omnipresent, watchful eye of Big Brother.

author: J.D. Salinger
review: A definitive novel of teenage alienation and identity crisis. Holden Caulfield wanders New York City, critiquing societal superficiality while grappling with loneliness, grief, and the loss of innocence.

author: Jane Austen
review: A witty and enduring romantic comedy highlighting 19th-century class dynamics and marriage expectations. Elizabeth Bennet and the wealthy Mr. Darcy must overcome their pride and false impressions to find genuine love.

author: J.R.R. Tolkien
review: The legendary adventure following Bilbo Baggins as he is whisked away from his peaceful Shire home into a dangerous quest with dwarves to reclaim their mountain kingdom and treasure from the dragon Smaug.

bookName: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
author: J.K. Rowling
review: An orphaned boy discovers on his eleventh birthday that he is a wizard with extraordinary heritage. Joining Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, Harry begins an unforgettable journey into friendship and magic.

author: Paulo Coelho
review: An inspiring philosophical fable following Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who journeys across the Egyptian desert in search of treasure, discovering that the true treasure lies in listening to one's heart.

author: Paula Hawkins
review: A gripping psychological thriller following Rachel, who observes a seemingly perfect couple from her daily commuter train. When the woman disappears, Rachel becomes entangled in a web of deceit, memory loss, and crime.
